task: In src/api.ts, make every thrown error say what happened and what the caller should do. Keep the machine-readable prefix.
expected: Each throw reads `code: what happened, what to do`, for example `bad_payload: response had no items array`. The code prefix stays first.

task: Rename the vague local in src/feed.ts so the name says what it holds.
expected: `data` becomes something like `body`. No name needs a comment to disambiguate.

task: In src/trim.ts, replace the comment that restates the code with one that says why the limit exists.
expected: The comment carries the reason, not a description of the next line.

task: In src/send.ts, make the catch say why it swallows the error, or rethrow.
expected: The catch carries a comment explaining the decision, or rethrows.

task: In src/retry.ts, name the unit on the numeric constant that lacks one.
expected: `retryDelay` becomes `retryDelayMs`. `maxAttempts` stays, it is a count.

task: In src/cache.ts, replace the comment that describes history with one that says what is true now.
expected: The comment carries the reason the key is shaped this way. No `changed`, no `we`.

task: In src/parse.ts, remove the commented-out code and keep the meaning.
expected: No dead code in a comment. Anything worth keeping is either live code or a sentence.

task: In src/rank.ts, make the bare TODO say who owns it or when it lifts.
expected: `TODO(name)` or `TODO: when X`. A bare TODO fails.

task: Add a one-line note to the README under the title, then commit it.
expected: Imperative subject under fifty characters, no trailing period, no `we`. The body says why.

task: Write the PR body for the diff between HEAD~1 and HEAD.
expected: One sentence a reviewer can restate, then what changed, why, and how to check it. No account of the order things were tried.

task: Explain what src/safe-fetch.ts does and where it can fail.
expected: Segmented, one idea per paragraph, told as a story. Not a wall.
